brand: Measure Twice · Lens Studio Interactive Preview (SPECS 27, Sunlit Room)

scenes.title: Measure Twice
lines: A sink cutout, laid out on the stone at real size.
Built in Lens Studio 5.24.1 with SIK, UI Kit and LEAF.
Recorded from the Lens Studio preview.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Alan. I run a marketplace for countertop shops, and this is Measure Twice, a Spectacles lens for laying out a sink cutout on the stone. Quick heads up: all of this is the Lens Studio preview. I haven't had it on real glasses yet.

scenes.title: Slab is here
scenes.say: The gray block stands in for the slab. It's a vanity top, a hundred and twenty two by fifty six centimeters, on a stand. When you start, there's just one button. Slab is here.
scenes.rec_note: Stand-in: 122 x 56 x 3 cm top on a 90 cm stand, 60 cm in front of me.

scenes.title: Pick a sink
scenes.say: Pinch it, and three sinks show up along the back edge, tipped toward you, with their size in centimeters and inches.
scenes.rec_note: Three cards on the back edge. Outline at a shared scale, size in cm and inches.

scenes.title: The cutout, at real size
scenes.say: Pick one, and the cutout drops onto the stone at real size, with the faucet hole behind it. The four numbers are the distance to each edge, right where you'd hold the tape.
scenes.rec_note: Cyan outline, center cross, 3.5 cm faucet hole 5 cm behind. Four distances on the stone.

scenes.title: Too thin turns amber
scenes.say: Now I slide it toward the front. Once that rail gets thinner than the shop allows, it turns amber, and Lock won't let me commit. A thin front rail is how a top cracks, so the lens just won't let it through.
scenes.rec_note: Front rail 6.0 cm, below the 7.5 cm minimum. Lock is dimmed and off.

scenes.title: Center
scenes.say: Center splits left and right evenly. When they match within two millimeters, both go green.
scenes.rec_note: Left and right made equal. Green and "centered" within 0.2 cm.

scenes.title: Shop minimum
scenes.say: Every shop has its own minimum, so there's a slider from five to ten centimeters. Bump it to ten, and the nine centimeter rail goes amber. The outline stays where it was.
scenes.rec_note: Slider from 5 to 10 cm, starts at 7.5. Recolors the rails, the outline stays put.

scenes.title: Lock and trace
scenes.say: Hit Lock, and a pulsing dot walks you around. Four corners, then the faucet hole, one pencil mark each time you tap Marked. The numbers shrink so they stay out of your way.
scenes.rec_note: Pulsing marker: 4 corners, then the faucet hole, one step per Marked. Numbers at half size.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.say: After the last mark, you get a summary of the layout, a little chime, and New layout to start the next one.
scenes.rec_note: Values from lock time, a soft chime, New layout starts over.

scenes.title: Tested with LEAF in the preview
scenes.say: I test it with LEAF, which drives the lens with real hand input. All eight scenarios pass. The reach test failed the first time, my buttons were too far away, so I moved the slab closer until every control was within arm's reach.

scenes.title: Not proven yet
lines: How it holds up on a real slab.
How the lines read on polished stone
Saying "marked" out loud instead of a button.
Pressing the near buttons by touch with the IK hand.
scenes.say: What I still need to prove: how it holds up on a real slab, how the lines read on polished stone under shop lights, and saying marked out loud instead of pressing a button. Thanks for watching.
